Favor of God
FAY-vuhr uhv GOD
doctrinal phrase
From Latin favor (good will, kindness) through Old French favour; the favor of God is His gracious good pleasure resting upon His people in Christ.

📖 Biblical Definition

The favor of God is His free, gracious good pleasure—the smile of His countenance resting upon those whom He loves in His Son. It is near kin to grace, for both name the unmerited kindness of God toward the undeserving, yet favor casts the warmth of a Father's pleasure over the relationship. The Psalmist sings, "For thou, LORD, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as with a shield"—the favor of God is a defense that surrounds the whole man. Solomon declares that whoso findeth wisdom "shall obtain favour of the LORD," for to find true wisdom is to find Christ Himself, in whom the Father is well pleased. This favor is no reward earned by merit; it flows from the eternal good pleasure of God, who chose His people before the foundation of the world and accepted them in the Beloved. Even our Lord in His true humanity "increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man," that the Mediator might secure for His people the favor He alone perfectly deserved. To stand in the favor of God is to live under the lifted light of His countenance, justified, adopted, and kept. The 1689 Confession traces every spiritual benefit to this fountain of free, unchanging divine good pleasure. The believer's confidence is not that he has earned a smile, but that the smile rests upon Christ, and upon him in Christ.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Kind regard; good will; the disposition to oblige or benefit. Of God, His gracious good pleasure and acceptance bestowed freely upon His people.

expand to see more

FAVOR, n. From Latin favor, good will, kindness; kind regard or benevolent disposition.

Kind regard; good will; countenance; the disposition to befriend, oblige, or benefit another.

Acceptance; the state of being approved and well-pleasing; the lifting up of one's countenance upon another.

Of God, His gracious good pleasure freely bestowed: "with favour wilt thou compass him as with a shield" (Ps 5:12).

A gift, kindness, or benefit conferred out of good will rather than owed as a debt.

📖 Key Scripture

Psa 5:12 — "For thou, LORD, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as with a shield."

Pro 8:35 — "For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the LORD."

Luk 2:52 — "And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man."

Psa 30:5 — "For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

No genuine postmodern redefinition besets this term; the recurring error is treating divine favor as wages for performance rather than free grace in Christ.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The favor of God is not so much twisted by ideology as cheapened by a works-righteousness that imagines God's smile must be purchased by sufficient effort, or by a presumption that takes His kindness for granted. Both forget that favor, like grace, is free and rests upon the merit of Another.

The principle to recover is that the favor of God flows from His eternal good pleasure and is secured for His people by Christ, who alone perfectly increased in favor with God. The believer is "accepted in the beloved," compassed about with favor as with a shield. The 1689 Confession grounds every blessing in this free and unchanging good pleasure—to walk in God's favor is to walk in the lifted light of His countenance, given, not earned.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Favor blends the Latin idea of benevolent good will with the biblical idea of free grace.

expand to see more

Latin favor — good will, kindness, support; source of "favorable" and "favorite."

Hebrew rāṣōn — good pleasure, acceptance, delight; the LORD's favorable regard.

Hebrew ḥēn — grace, favor, charm; the unmerited kindness shown to the lowly.

Greek charis — grace, favor; the New Testament word uniting favor and grace.

"Favour" in the KJV often translates the same words rendered elsewhere as "grace."

Usage

"Doctrinally, the favor of God is closely allied to grace and to the doctrine of free acceptance in Christ."

"Pastorally, it assures the saint that God's countenance is lifted upon him for Christ's sake."

"Devotionally, it answers the Aaronic blessing—"the LORD lift up his countenance upon thee.""
